propositions: The DC harness errored all 62 cells at fixture setup because a session-start field-readiness gate waits for Epic Link and Epic Name fields, which are only provisioned by GreenHopper when the first Jira Software project is created, creating a deadlock where the gate blocks the action that would create the fields it waits for.

Experiment 30981084637 proved the root cause is ordering, not budget: field inventory remained unchanged after 180s of quiet waiting (27 fields, 0 customfield_*), but appeared within 0.05s of creating a GreenHopper scrum project (55 fields, 13 customfield_*).

The decision rule in not_ready_message ('zero customfield_* entries means plugin is still starting, budget is too short') is self-confirming and wrong: an empty custom-field inventory is the normal state of a Jira instance with no project, and this rule misdiagnosed the actual ordering defect.

The fix moves the Epic-field capability check from session-start (wait_for_jira_dc_ready) to post-provisioning (_assert_project_capabilities), where those fields can actually exist, and relocates the probe's _await_named_fields to run after project creation.

Live verification run 30982731669 achieved 62 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed, 0 errored, with field registration measurements (0.032s-0.058s per project) supporting the 120s allowance sized from the measured 0.0512s provisioning time.
